Tinker's depot rules and the oil patch: NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A for Oklahoma City NDT technicians

At Tinker Air Force Base the NDT personnel rules are published. Air Force Sustainment Center Instruction 20-114, Qualification of Nondestructive Inspection Personnel (January 2024, with Change 1 in January 2025), is the written practice for NDI personnel at the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex and the other Air Force depots. It sets their qualification and certification per NAS 410 and says that where the instruction and NAS 410 conflict, the text of NAS 410 takes precedence. That makes Oklahoma City unusual: the depot, one of the biggest concentrations of aerospace NDT work in the central US, runs on the aerospace standard, while the oil and gas economy around it runs on written practices built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

What the depot instruction means for contractors

The instruction says certification is employer based and that the depot has no mechanism to certify contract personnel. Before contract NDI personnel work inside the Complex or on Complex workload, the contractor submits its written practice and each inspector's qualification and certification records for review, and people who do not meet the NAS 410 training and certification requirements are not allowed to perform NDI there. At each Complex the ALC NDI Program Manager acts as the Responsible Level 3. In plain terms, if your employer sends you onto Tinker work, your certification has to come from a program built to NAS 410, and your file has to survive a depot review.

Contractors around the base and civil work at Will Rogers

Boeing's Oklahoma City site modernizes and modifies military aircraft, including the B-52 and B-1 bombers and AWACS, and suppliers across the metro make and repair parts for depot and defense programs; defense purchase orders commonly flow NAS 410 down from the prime. The Air Force has also broken ground at Tinker on a hangar for future B-21 maintenance, which points to more of the same work ahead. Civil repair stations near Will Rogers World Airport follow whatever standard their own manuals and customer contracts name. The FAA's Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center is in the city, yet the FAA does not certify NDT personnel; its advisory circular AC 65-31B lists NAS 410, ATA Specification 105 and SNT-TC-1A among acceptable standards.

Oil, gas and wind under SNT-TC-1A

SCOOP and STACK production facilities, gathering and transmission lines running toward Cushing, gas plants and wind tower construction inspect to API 1104, the ASME B31 codes and AWS D1.1. Contractors on that side certify under written practices built on SNT-TC-1A. A UT and MT Level II from oilfield work is solid evidence, but a depot reviewer or a supplier's RL3 will still measure it against NAS 410, and most will ask for more formal penetrant and magnetic particle training first, because the surface methods are where NAS 410 goes furthest beyond SNT-TC-1A's recommendations.

Checklist for an oilfield technician eyeing aerospace work

  • Ask the hiring Level 3 which standard and revision govern, and whether the job touches Complex workload.
  • Gather course outlines with recorded hours, an experience log signed for each method, your examination history and a current vision record.
  • Expect to be certified again; nothing transfers between employers except evidence.
  • Learn fluorescent penetrant and eddy current early, since they dominate engine and airframe inspection.

Contractors serving both the depot and energy customers should state the governing standard and revision on every certification, keep training files to the NAS 410 level of evidence, and plan the move to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, with their customers and any depot program they support.

Atlantis in Oklahoma City

Atlantis training is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory with Q&A from our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), rehearsal in the Practical NDT aircraft hangar, and the hands-on practical at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Oklahoma City. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Oklahoma City contractors, and it is not a route onto depot NDI work. Whether outside training counts toward a NAS 410 certification is your employer's RL3's call, so ask before enrolling. Contractors preparing records for a customer or Nadcap audit can use NAS 410 audit documentation support and Level III audit support for aerospace, with the RL3 approving every document. Read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 explained; for methods, see penetrant testing training and eddy current testing in aviation.
